analysis.title: GS Commods | US Power Biweekly
key_insights: PJM power saw elevated volatility after the midterm elections as markets reacted to policy rhetoric and data center moratorium proposals across the Lower 48.
Longer-dated PJM contracts sold off aggressively, led by Summer 28 through Cal31. Spark spreads dropped about 20% from their peaks amid regulatory and interconnection uncertainty, then normalized.

Ohio is the focal point of the PJM debate. Scrutiny centers less on operating data centers and more on whether planned multi-gigawatt pipelines face permitting hurdles, local bans or tariff-driven delays.
The PJM prompt market is very strong because of an unseasonable cold snap across the east. Cash spark spreads are significantly higher and spot power is clearing at triple digits.
Strength in Dec-Feb and Cal27 pushed Cal27 spark spreads back toward contract highs, which sharply steepened curve backwardation across PJM.
ERCOT bore the initial brunt of the post-election sell-off, with Summer 28 and outer years repricing lower on data center moratorium rhetoric and scrutiny of large load interconnections.
The ERCOT curve rebounded across several hubs this week. Participants see significant uncertainty over actual statutory implementation and grandfathering carveouts, despite the moratorium headlines.
Cash spark spreads rallied across Texas and into the West as wind and solar output dropped during high-demand intervals.

The ERCOT medium-term curve is caught between large battery and solar additions and industrial and AI demand growth. The prompt market shows vulnerability to generation swings, which gives a firm near-term floor.

sector_views.rationale: Prompt power is strong on cold weather and low renewable output, while long-dated curves are pressured by data center moratorium and interconnection uncertainty. The note describes market moves and does not state a sector rating.

risk_factors: Data center moratorium proposals and policy rhetoric could slow large load growth and weigh on long-dated power prices.
Permitting hurdles, local bans or tariff-driven delays could hit planned multi-gigawatt data center pipelines, with Ohio the focus.
Unclear statutory implementation and grandfathering carveouts for large load interconnection in ERCOT.
Battery and solar additions against industrial and AI demand growth add uncertainty to the ERCOT medium-term curve.
Prompt power prices are exposed to weather and swings in wind and solar generation.
